Skip the assignment prompt when nothing fits

The game raises "Resource Assignments Available" when a Resource reaches your pool, or when a Settlement gains a slot. It is high priority and does not expire at end of turn, so it holds the end-turn button until you act on it - even when there is nothing you could do.[N][N]With this on, the prompt is not drawn while nothing you hold could legally be placed anywhere, including when all that is left is a Factory Resource and no Settlement with a free slot has a Factory. It returns the moment that changes. Nothing is dismissed and turn blocking is untouched; only the drawing is declined.[N][N]Also requires automatic assignment to be on: with it off the mod places nothing for you, so the prompt is telling you something you still need to act on.

Before anything else, assignment tries to lift Settlements out of negative Happiness, worst first. This outranks Factories, Camels and each Settlement's own priority, so it is the largest single thing the mod does to a layout.

Every Resource that pays Culture - Turtles, Silk, Mangos, Flax, Wine, Incense and whatever else the age offers - is gathered into the one City that already makes the most Culture on its own, instead of being scattered. Several of them are percentages, so a percentage of one big number beats the same percentage of six small ones. Settlements you have given a priority of their own are served first, and only what is left over gets gathered.

The same for Gold: Jade, Cowrie, Rubies, Silver, Cloves and the rest are gathered into the City that already makes the most Gold - and deliberately not the Culture one, so the two piles do not compete for the same slots. Settlements you have given a priority of their own are served first.
Don't show tooltips on the Commerce screen

With this on, none of the explanations this mod adds to the Commerce screen are drawn: the framed tooltips on its own buttons, switches and settlement controls, the plain ones on its bars, totals, padlocks and trade-route titles, and the extended resource tooltip on the Empire, Factory and Treasure cards. The round "?" marks go with them, since a mark exists only to carry a tooltip.[N][N]The game's OWN tooltips are untouched - they are not this mod's to take away.[N][N]Off by default. The explanations are the point of most of what this mod adds; this is for the player who has read them and wants the screen quiet.[N][N]Takes full effect the next time the Commerce screen is opened.

Assigns Resources that reached you over a Trade Route from another leader before any of your own, and only into Cities.[N][N]Why it pays: towards an [B]Economic Victory[/B] a Resource slotted in a City is worth +1 GDP per turn, and an imported one is worth +1 more on top of that - twice as much as your own. Neither pays anything in a Town, so imports are never sent to one.[N][N][B]Only worth it for the Economic Victory.[/B] It outranks every Settlement's own priority, so until the last import is placed your Cities take whatever the trade network happens to supply instead of what you told them to specialise in. Chasing Culture, Science or a Military win, leave this off.
